title: Sharding: the shard key, the balancer, and the key you cannot change later

videos.script: A replica set gives you three copies of everything. It does not give you more room. {{copies}} When the data outgrows one machine, you cut a collection into ranges and spread them over several replica sets. Each one is a shard. {{shards}} In front of them sits a router, mongos. Behind it, a config server keeps the map of which range lives where. {{router}} You will build that cluster with one short script, on the same machine as everything else. {{script}} Then the decision that matters. The shard key. Pick an order number that only ever grows, and every new order lands on the same shard. The other one sits idle. {{hot}} Pick a hashed key, and the orders spread evenly. But now a range of order numbers has to ask every shard. {{hashed}} You will watch the balancer move data between shards. And you will give it a key with a single value, and watch it give up. {{jumbo}} Last, the key you cannot change later. You can, these days. It just costs a copy of the whole collection, and you will time one. {{reshard}}
